history.ask: Colicky pain radiating loin to groin
Urethral discharge or new sexual contact

options: Hesitancy, weak stream, nocturia, terminal dribbling

history.ask: Perineal or low back pain with fever (men)
Weight loss, night sweats, or TB history/contact
Catheter, recent urological procedure, or known stones

red_flags: Fever with rigors and flank pain — ascending infection with sepsis risk
Inability to pass urine (acute retention) or anuria
Fever with urinary symptoms in pregnancy
Vomiting with inability to keep fluids down plus reduced urine output
exam: Temperature and full vital signs — quantify systemic upset
Percuss and press over both renal angles for tenderness
Percuss and palpate for a distended bladder
Inspect external genitalia: urethral discharge in men, vulvovaginal inflammation or discharge in women
Gentle digital rectal exam in men: exquisitely tender boggy prostate (prostatitis) vs smooth symmetric enlargement (BPH)
Look for cachexia or pallor when symptoms are chronic

investigations.why: Nitrites with pyuria rule bacterial cystitis/pyelonephritis in; RBCs point to stone or tumor; persistent sterile pyuria points to genitourinary TB or urethritis; candida appears in diabetics
Confirms the organism — indicated for fever, all men, recurrence, pregnancy, or failed empirical course
Leukocytosis supports pyelonephritis or acute prostatitis over simple cystitis
Detects renal impairment from obstruction, stones, or sepsis — changes disposition
Uncovers uncontrolled diabetes behind recurrent infection or candidal dysuria
Screens the pregnancy red flag and reframes any febrile urinary infection as high-risk
Shows hydronephrosis or stone behind colicky pain, prostate size and residual volume in obstructive symptoms, and any bladder mass
If discharge is present: confirms urethritis (STI) or vulvovaginitis as the cause of dysuria without bacteriuria
If chronic symptoms with sterile pyuria, weight loss, or TB contact: rules genitourinary tuberculosis in
Second-line — for visible painless hematuria at age > 40: rules bladder carcinoma in or out

supports: Burning frequency and urgency without fever or flank pain
Fever with rigors and loin pain
Perineal or low back pain with fever in a man
Gradual hesitancy, weak stream, nocturia in an older man
External burning rather than deep dysuria
Chronic frequency > 4 weeks unresponsive to antibiotic courses
Weight loss, night sweats, or TB contact
